definitions.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

definitions.type: unmodified time-step map and finite numerical trajectories
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps>0, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

definitions.type: smooth-input trilinear averaged cubic remainder with a polynomial dense core
definitions.definition: For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I with length at most one, X(I) consists of L^infinity(I;L^2) functions with weak time derivative in L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)); ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L^2))+||f'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). All time suprema of continuous functions use their continuous representatives; derivatives and L^infinity norms use essential suprema.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

inputs.statement: The following estimates have constants uniform in the real time t. For mean-zero f in L^2, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2. For any A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). For f,g in L^2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0 with Dinv A0 in L^2 and g in L^2, ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2 and ||J_t(A0,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2. For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Ctri_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise and sum across internal endpoints for continuous piecewise smooth paths. For time-independent mean-zero f,g, Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t). The bounded products extend from polynomials by density.

inputs.statement: With normalized norms, for every interval I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b<=a+1 and continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero paths f_j, ||Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C|I|product_j||f_j||_(X(I))+C||f_i||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)))product_(j!=i)||f_j||_(L^infinity(I;L^2)), for each slot i=1,2,3. For time-independent mean-zero H^sigma inputs, 0<=sigma<=1, ||Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C_sigma|I|^sigma product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma). For 0<gamma<=1 set a_gamma=1/2-gamma when gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 when gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 when gamma>1/2. Then a_gamma in [0,1), ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)). For every M0>=0, mean-zero w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, 0<tau<=1, a>=0, and a<=t<=a+tau, ||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma and ||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0). Constants are uniform in a,t,tau and Fourier support. Ctri and stages extend by their stated bounds.

inputs.statement: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is a continuous map on the real mean-zero L^2 space, preserves mean zero and reality, and maps smooth data to smooth data; Ftau:L^2->H^1 is continuous. Hence all finite numerical trajectories are defined and continuous in the initial datum. For every smooth mean-zero real f, tau>0 and integer n>=0, S_(-(n+1)*tau)Psi_tau(S_(n*tau)f)=f+Fstage_(n*tau,(n+1)*tau)(f)+integral_(n*tau)^((n+1)*tau)B_s(f,Fstage_(n*tau,s)(f))ds-Rem_(n*tau,tau)(f,f,f). Consequently on a numerical smooth trajectory the tuple Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n) has Vst(t_n)=v^n and Vst(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1). The interpolants therefore concatenate to a continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero real V on [0,T].

For 0<gamma<=1, M0>=1, a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero real f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, put q=tau^gamma+delta and (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y)=Interp_(a,tau;f), I=[a,a+tau]. Constants C_(gamma,M0) below are uniform in a,tau and all higher norms or spectral supports. Then ||f||_2<=M0+1, q<=2, sup_I||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta, sup_I(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, ||z||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, sup_I||Q||_2+||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and sup_I||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Here a_gamma is 1/2-gamma,1/8,0 in the respective cases gamma<1/2, gamma=1/2, gamma>1/2. Moreover Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau, sup_I||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, sup_I||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f), sup_I||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, and sup_I||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

output.statement: For 0<gamma<=1, M0>=1, a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero real f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and ||f-w||_2<=1, put q=tau^gamma+||f-w||_2 and take the tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y)=Interp_(a,tau;f); define rho(t)=-integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds-(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(Y,Y)ds-((t-a)/tau)*W on [a,a+tau]. Then Vst'=(1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst)+rho', rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau, sup||rho||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. On a smooth numerical trajectory and smooth exact twisted solution v with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, concatenate these increments into Rres(0)=0, and let V be its continuous concatenation with grid values V(t_n)=v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. Then V'=(1/2)B_t(V,V)+Rres'. If I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, including an endpoint inside a step, one has sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0). The constants are independent of grid index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

argument.text: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. First fix a step with the antecedent L1 of N008: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, with smooth real mean-zero f,w, M0>=1 and the stated a,tau. Use its tuple and q. Differentiation of Interp gives Vst'=(1/2)B_t(z,z)-W/tau. Since Vst=z+Y, subtraction of (1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst) gives rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau. The residual increment vanishes at a. N008 bounds ||Y||_2 by C*q, ||z||_2 by C and ||W||_2/tau by C*q, with q<=2. N005 thus gives ||rho'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, Vst'=(1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst)+rho', rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau, and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: For the first integral in rho apply N005's normal form to (Y,z). Its boundary J terms are O(tau*q) using ||Dinv Y||_2<=C*tau*q from N008 and bounded ||z||_2. The integral containing Y' is O(tau*q) by the asymmetric J bound and ||Dinv Y'||_2<=C*q. Since z'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), symmetry turns the remaining term into a fixed multiple of Ctri_[a,t](f,f,Y). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y: N008 gives ||Y||_X<=C*q and ||Y||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q, while f is constant with L^2 norm <=M0+1. Hence this term too is O(tau*q), even on a partial step.

For integral B(Y,Y), apply the same normal form with Y in both slots. Boundary terms use ||Dinv Y||_2||Y||_2<=C*tau*q^2, and derivative integrals use ||Dinv Y'||_2||Y||_2<=C*q^2 over length tau. Thus it is O(tau*q^2)=O(tau*q) because q<=2. The affine W term is O(tau*q) by N008. Combine with F001-F002 to prove both residual estimates on the whole or any initial part of the step. Discharge L1 and quantify the data.

produces.statement: For every Mbar>=1,a0>=0,0<tau1<=1 and smooth real mean-zero f0,w0 with ||w0||_(H^gamma)<=Mbar and ||f0-w0||_2<=1, let q0=tau1^gamma+||f0-w0||_2 and let Y0,z0,W0,V0 be the corresponding components of Interp_(a0,tau1;f0). Define rho0(t)=-integral_a0^t B_s(Y0,z0)ds-(1/2)integral_a0^t B_s(Y0,Y0)ds-((t-a0)/tau1)W0. On [a0,a0+tau1], V0'=(1/2)B_t(V0,V0)+rho0', rho0'=-B_t(Y0,z0)-(1/2)B_t(Y0,Y0)-W0/tau1, sup||rho0||_2<=C_(gamma,Mbar)*tau1*q0 and ||rho0'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,Mbar)*q0.

argument.text: Now fix a smooth numerical trajectory and exact twisted v and assume L2: sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h<=1 and E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. N007 gives the continuous interpolation V with grid values v^n. Concatenate the residual increments, obtaining Rres and V'=(1/2)B(V,V)+Rres' stepwise and distributionally. At each intersected step start t_n, delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I, so its q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I and F003 applies with w=v(t_n),f=v^n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps; the last can be partial. Sum the step increment bounds to obtain sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also sup||Rres'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

Under L2, ||v||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0 and ||V||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0+1. Subtract the equations to obtain e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 and F004 imply ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), so ||e||_X has the same bound. The exact equation bounds ||v'||_(H^(-pstar)), and V=v-e then has bounded X norm too, since tau^gamma+E_I<=2. This proves the remaining assertions. Discharge L2 and quantify the trajectory and interval.
